conviction_note: The release carries Ambu's FIRST FY2026/27 guide, a scheduled guidance event on a stock whose last two annual-report days moved -8.7% and -15.8%, so abs_move is 9.0. Direction is nearly balanced. The baseline missed a crowded 6.08% disclosed short (a register join defect), which leans up. Against it: two guidance cuts this year, a Q4 the company itself said needs a stronger quarter, and a +32% rally off the September low that Danish medtech peers matched. p_up is therefore 51. The findings sum to +0.9 against a scaled +0.18 because the positioning finding is sized on its own and the sign of the guide, where the move lives, has no sourced bar.

new_in_release.expect: FIRST FY2026/27 guide, where the move lives. Direction unknown. The anchors are the 11-13% long-term organic CAGR and the path to a +20% margin by FY29/30. Last year's first guide (10-13% organic, 12-14% margin) was met with -15.8%. A margin guide that lifts as the IEEPA tariff headwind falls away would be the upside case; organic guided below 10% on A&PM would be the downside case.

Q4 organic has to be about 12-14% to reach '~10%' for the year off 9M at 8.7%, against an easy 10.0% comparison. Expect FY at roughly 9.5-10%, a small miss risk. Q4 EBIT margin is inflated by the DKK 85m refund, so FY EBIT should land around 13.5-14%. Upside if any of the further DKK 155m is recognised.
unknown; inventory was elevated through FY24/25 and FY25/26 for tariff mitigation; the long-term cash-conversion target of +40% is the bar

findings.finding: Ambu carries a 6.08% aggregated disclosed net short (03-11-2026), the 4th-largest in Denmark. The sealed baseline recorded it as 0.0 because of a name-join defect. Sellers covered only about 0.7pt from the 6.78% peak on 19-10 while the stock rose about 30%, so a crowded, underwater short sits into a first-guide print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed squeeze event on Ambu in the sources read. On print days with a positive guide the name has jumped (+9.29% on the 1 Oct 2025 session after the ZOOM AHEAD targets; +8.95% on 8 Nov 2023), consistent with short fuel. Negative guides were not cushioned (-15.8% on 5 Nov 2025, -15.75% on 26 Aug 2026).
findings.why_not_priced: The sealed baseline and its priced_lean_pct carry 0.0 for short_squeeze, so this stage's own lean omits it. The shorts are known to the market. What is unpriced is the asymmetry: a 6% short that has covered only ~10% of itself through a 32% rally would show as a register falling toward 4-5% if it were being unwound ahead of the print, and it has not.
findings.independence: researcher_europe/analysis/eu-short-cache.json (dk, 'AMBU A S': 6.62 -> 6.78 -> 6.10 -> 6.00 -> 5.98 -> 6.08, 13-10 to 03-11) is a separate daily read of the same register, so not independent of the register

findings.finding: The Q4 EBIT margin is inflated by a DKK 85m IEEPA tariff refund received after Q3 and booked in Q4, about 5pt of Q4 margin. A further DKK 155m was due and not booked as of 25 Aug, so FY EBIT b.s.i. could print above the 14% top of the guide if any of it is recognised.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior refund line at Ambu. The European worked case (H&M, which beat with a tariff refund inside and fell 2%) says the market looks through this.
findings.original_quote: Ambu venter nu driftsmarginen i den høje ende af 12 % til 14 % (Ambu now expects the operating margin at the high end of 12% to 14%); the note records DKK 85m received after quarter-end and booked in Q4, with DKK 155m still due and not booked
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company already guided 'toward the high end' because of it. What is not priced is the second DKK 155m tranche. If the market expected it inside FY25/26 EBIT, consensus would sit above 14%, and the only public read (HCA) has 12.4% moving to the high end.
findings.independence: https://www.inderes.dk/en/releases/interim-report-for-q3 (company: 'First refunds received of IEEPA tariffs, with reclaim process ongoing'; tariff refunds 'supporting the upper end')

findings.finding: Reaching the '~10%' FY organic guide off 8.7% for 9M needs roughly 12-14% organic growth in Q4, against 10.3% in Q3. The company has cut the growth guide twice this year (10-13% to 10-12% on 6 May, to ~10% on 25 Aug), so a 9.x% outturn is a live risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Growth-guide cuts were punished: -3.70% on 6 May 2026 and -15.75% on 26 Aug 2026 (Yahoo daily closes). The Q4 comparison is easier (Q4 24/25 organic 10.0% against 12.0% in Q3).
findings.original_quote: hvilket kræver et stærkere fjerde kvartal (which requires a stronger fourth quarter)
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the guide was set on 25 Aug with July and most of August in hand, which makes a large miss unlikely, so it sits inside what the company guided. If the market feared a miss, the stock would have lagged its Danish medtech peers since September. It matched them (+32% against Coloplast +22.6% and Demant +21.2%).

findings.finding: Ambu's +32% rally from the 21 Sep low (DKK 64.65 to about 86) is mostly Danish medtech beta, not a rise in expectations for Ambu's own guide. Over the same period Coloplast is +22.6%, Demant +21.2% and the OMXC25 +9.5%, and no Ambu-specific release, upgrade or press item from October was found.
findings.why_not_priced: The free control (-run_up_20d) and priced_lean (-1.1) read the +22% 20-day run-up as idiosyncratic and due to mean-revert. If it were an Ambu-specific expectations build, Ambu would have outrun its peers and the Nasdaq Nordic feed would show company news. It roughly matched the sector, and the feed shows no Ambu release from 22 Oct to 3 Nov. This is a proxy inference, so it is sized small.
